title: Comparison of 4 experiments
disclaimer: Planet-like predictions are research leads, not discoveries: a high score means the light-curve shape resembles signals that NASA vetting classified as planet candidates, nothing more.

experiments.title: Experiment report: Standard DR24 - Logistic regression
experiments.disclaimer: Planet-like predictions are research leads, not discoveries: a high score means the light-curve shape resembles signals that NASA vetting classified as planet candidates, nothing more.

model_card.name: Logistic regression
model_card.description: A linear classifier on standardised view bins and physical features. It weighs each input independently, so it shows how much of the problem is solvable without learned shape detectors.
inputs: Physical features measured from the light curve (depth, duration, SNR, odd/even, secondary eclipse, shape, scatter...). No catalogue scores or dispositions.

data_provenance.label_mode_description: DR24 TCE av_training_set: PC -> planet-like (1); AFP, NTP -> false-positive-like (0); UNK or no TCE -> excluded (Shallue & Vanderburg 2018).

experiments.limitations: These results describe how well a model separates Kepler transit-like signals labelled planet-like from those labelled false-positive-like by published NASA vetting, on star-separated held-out data processed by this application's pipeline. Labels are expert/automated judgements and contain noise; class 0 mixes astrophysical false positives and non-transiting phenomena. Photometry alone cannot rule out background eclipsing binaries or contamination (no pixel or centroid data are used). Models are trained on Kepler long-cadence data only; other missions or cadences are out of distribution. Small datasets give wide confidence intervals, so differences between models inside overlapping intervals are not evidence of a real difference.

model_card.name: Random forest
model_card.description: An ensemble of decision trees on the same inputs as logistic regression. Trees capture non-linear rules and interactions between diagnostics without feature scaling.

model_card.name: Single-view CNN (global view)
model_card.description: AstroNet's global-view network: a 1-D convolutional column reads the whole phase-folded orbit (2001 bins) and learns shape detectors for transits, secondary eclipses and variability.
model_card.reference: Shallue, C. J. & Vanderburg, A. (2018), Identifying Exoplanets with Deep Learning, AJ 155, 94

experiments.title: Experiment report: Standard DR24 - Two-view CNN (AstroNet)
experiments.disclaimer: Planet-like predictions are research leads, not discoveries: a high score means the light-curve shape resembles signals that NASA vetting classified as planet candidates, nothing more.

model_card.name: Two-view CNN (AstroNet)
model_card.description: The AstroNet architecture: a global column reads the whole folded orbit and a local column zooms on the transit (+/- 2 durations, 201 bins); their features are combined by fully-connected layers. This design found Kepler-90 i and Kepler-80 g.
model_card.reference: Shallue, C. J. & Vanderburg, A. (2018), Identifying Exoplanets with Deep Learning, AJ 155, 94
